so.text: When a move was made shows whether it was planned or a year-end adjustment. In FY2026 most of the money moved in the last five weeks.

blocks.title: Every recorded move, dated

paragraphs.text: **Voted above cost** is the vote, less what the line cost from every fund. **Paid by other funds** is what grants, the circuit breaker, fees and revolving funds paid toward the line. **Transfers** moved budget between lines. **Another year’s money** is orders carried in from last year, less what they paid, less next year’s bills paid early.

Which other-fund dollar counts toward which line is our reading, in order: a journal entry naming both ends, then the same payee, then the same function code (placed on a category, never a line). What none of them places is shown apart, never counted as voted above cost. Capital articles are matched only by a journal entry.

so.text: Open any line to see why it ended where it did, and which fund paid what toward it, with the rule that matched each payment.

blocks.title: Every line, in four parts

note.text: The first two steps are our placing of other funds’ spending; their sum is measured. The last two are postings. School general fund, department 300.

chart.title: From the vote to what was left

so.text: A line is what is left after other funds pay, so it can end under with nothing costing less. They paid $394,851 more than in FY2025.

conclusions.text: Other funds paid $1,636,899 toward FY2026’s lines; the vote alone was $1,019,800 below what they cost.

so.text: One grant changed payer both ways in one year; the voted budget shows neither. Why it paid the placement is in no document held.

conclusions.text: The IDEA grant paid $287,108 of private tuition; June entries moved $205,645 of its pay onto the general fund.

so.text: A swing of $620,281 between two years, made by entries after the spending. Each is in the journal with its date and memo.

conclusions.text: Journal entries took a net $366,899 off the general fund in FY2026, after adding $253,382 in FY2025.

so.text: Without the early payment FY2026 would have left $671,395, more than FY2025 on the same footing.

conclusions.text: FY2026 paid $189,277 of FY2027 tuition; $41,377 of FY2025’s orders were carried in and never paid.

finding.text: FY2026’s lines left $482,118; other funds paid $1,636,899 of their cost, $394,851 more than in FY2025.

not_established: Whether any other-fund payment replaced general fund spending or added to it: the books record who paid, not what would have happened otherwise.
Which line a function-code match belongs to: it is placed on a category only.
